observations.content: search queries over 500ms are considered slow per the platform SLA. Current p95 is 800ms, well above threshold.
the search index was last rebuilt 3 days ago (full reindex). Prior to that, the last rebuild was 6 months ago.
search latency has been degrading steadily over the past 2 weeks, not correlated with index age.
elasticsearch cluster has 3 data nodes, 500GB total disk, running ES 8.11.
index size is 200GB across 50 shards. Shard distribution is even across nodes.
cluster health is green. No pending tasks, no unassigned shards.
JVM heap usage on all nodes is between 60-70%, within recommended range.
rebuilding the search index has historically fixed slow query performance in 4 out of 4 past incidents.
index rebuild procedure: POST /_reindex with source=products-v* and dest=products-v{next}. Takes ~45 minutes.
index rebuild is the standard first response in the search performance runbook.
September 2025: search p95 hit 1200ms. Index rebuild resolved the issue, p95 dropped to 200ms.
June 2025: search p95 hit 900ms after a large bulk import. Index rebuild resolved the issue.
January 2025: search latency spike after mapping change. Index rebuild fixed it.
August 2024: first documented search performance incident. Index rebuild was the fix.
some queries use expensive wildcard patterns (leading wildcards like *keyword*) on the description field, which bypass the inverted index.
query caching is disabled in production. The request cache and query cache are both set to 0% of heap.
adding a keyword sub-field to description and rewriting wildcard queries as term queries could reduce latency by 60-80%.
enabling the request cache (indices.requests.cache.size: 2%) could help for repeated queries.
index rebuild was attempted 3 days ago by the SRE team and completed successfully in 42 minutes. No errors reported.
after the rebuild completed, p95 latency remained at 800ms. The rebuild had no measurable impact on search performance.
SRE team concluded: 'the current performance issue is not caused by index fragmentation or stale mappings. Root cause is elsewhere.'
